description:
Twelve tokens, each a single radially symmetric burst of tapered lozenge shapes radiating from one central point, floating dead centre on a near-black charcoal ground with generous empty margin all round. It is unmistakably a picture OF something: a flower head seen from directly overhead - the chrysanthemum / aster / dandelion / cornflower family. Not abstract, not architectural, not machine-like. A botanical plate rendered on black.

Made of: concentric rings of elongated rounded-end petals set at regular angular intervals, each ring rotated slightly against the last, drawn with soft partial opacity so overlaps read as translucent layering rather than hard occlusion. Outer rings are mid-to-dark neutral grey and sit behind like cast shadow or a second row of petals; the mass of the head is cream / bone / ivory; the core is a small disc of sage-olive green short strokes, sometimes with a pale pip at the exact centre. Several seeds (1283437, 1985692, 1991107) scatter tiny dark-green dashes over the white mass and fling a few outside the head entirely, reading as pollen or spent stamens.

Palette is very narrow and clearly deliberate: near-black ground, one cream family, one neutral grey family, one sage-green accent. There is no hue contrast anywhere in the collection - the whole thing is value-driven, and the black ground supports rather than competes.

What the twelve share: dead-centre placement, full radial symmetry, the same petal vocabulary, the same three colour families, the same soft opacity layering, the same black field. They read as one herbarium plate set.

How they differ: SCALE - 1283437 and 1835793 are small tight buttons occupying under half the tile, while 1985692, 1991107 and 1243682 nearly fill it. DENSITY - 1243682 is spiky and open with wide black gaps between separated outer petals, whereas 1985692 and 1991107 are near-solid discs with almost no ground showing inside the head. PETAL SHAPE - 1446330 and 1561509 run to long needles; 1985692 and 1991107 to broad rounded blades. CORE - 1203347, 1475115 and especially 1733538 carry a large dominant green centre; the rest show only a small green eye. 1733538 is the outlier of the set: a compact ragged green star with white flecks thrown around it and very little white petal mass, closer to a splash or a moss rosette than to a flower head.

Across the three market states (shown for 1203347, 1243682, 1283437, 1310661): the change is real but it is a hue-and-spread change, not a structural one. Stress consistently ADDS GREEN and pushes petals apart or outward - 1283437 grows a distinct outer ring of green blade petals under stress, the single clearest state change on the sheet; 1243682 opens its core into a large green pinwheel and its outer ring lightens to cream; 1203347 parts its petals and shows green between them; 1310661 gets green shading through the middle band. Recovery consistently returns a fuller, denser, slightly greener-cored version of neutral - 1203347 recovery is visibly the fullest and greenest of its three. Nothing darkens, nothing fractures, nothing wilts or breaks apart. If anything the stress frames look livelier and healthier than neutral, because green reads as growth here.

At 120px the twelve still read as twelve, but not evenly. Scale, open-vs-dense, and the big green cores all survive: 1283437, 1835793, 1243682, 1733538, 1203347 and 1475115 are each identifiable at browse size. Three collapse into one another - 1366079, 1446330 and 1561509 are all just 'medium spiky cream burst with grey outer petals' at 120, and 1985692 and 1991107 are near-identical big dense cream discs. Fine texture - the green flecks, the centre pip, the grey shadow layering - turns to mush and the inner mass becomes a flat cream blob. On the 120 state sheet, 1283437 stress and 1243682 stress read clearly and 1203347 recovery reads as fuller, but 1310661's three states are very close and I would not reliably tell them apart at that size.

Artifacts: no clipping anywhere - every head sits well inside its tile with margin, nothing meets the viewBox edge, nothing is cut in half. Overlaps are soft and read as intended layering rather than collision. The loose flecks outside the head on 1733538 read more like stray noise than form. The centres of 1283437 and 1835793 are slightly muddled clusters. Compositionally there is one move made twelve times: a centred stamp, radial, symmetrical, floating, with the frame itself entirely unused - no asymmetry, no off-centre weight, no edge play.
